utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, everybody, and welcome. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record accused Beara is not present today. He's still sick. I take it the waiver carries on today as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I spoke to him this morning and we're supposed to get a second waiver soon, sometime this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you are confirming it, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am, yes. I spoke to him this morning and he has given his consent to proceed without him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I see that Mr. Meek is absent. That's about it. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Nicholls, Mr. Thayer. The witness is also present in the courtroom. Now, as you may have noticed, Judge Stole is not with us today for personal reasons, therefore, we are proceeding with the sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are testifying pursuant to the solemn declaration that you made yesterday that you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning. I want to turn your attention to July 1995. Can you estimate approximately how many able-bodied Muslim men there were in the Zepa area at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in July 1995, if we say that men between 18 and 60 are able-bodied men -- well, according to the information that I have, according to the situation that prevailed, there were about 1.200 men, perhaps a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how many of those men would you say were armed at this time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again I don't have precise and detailed information, but I would say that there were between 6 and 700 armed men.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Colonel Avdo Palic was their commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Avdo Palic was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when the Zepa safe area was established in 1993, it was supposed to be militarised; is that correct? Or demilitarised. Forgive me.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But it wasn't fully demilitarised, was it, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, most of the weapons were handed over, but since many of the weapons were the personal property of certain individuals, I assume that they were retained and weren't handed over to the UNPROFOR base in Zepa. Only light infantry weapons were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you aware, sir, that arms and ammunition were reaching the enclave despite the demilitarisation agreement?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had, in the second half of 1994, weapons were delivered by helicopter, as well as ammunition. They were delivered to the Zepa sector. I don't have any information about the quantity of weapons concerned or the kind of weapons, but I'm aware of this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, prior to the VRS assault on the Srebrenica enclave, did you learn about certain military operations which were undertaken by Commander Palic's men?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about one such operation. I can't remember the exact date, but I think it was in mid-June. There was an attack outside the Zepa area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you become aware as to what the objective of that military operation was at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, it was to take the pressure off the Sarajevo battlefield. As far as I know, action was carried out to lift the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to get a little bit more specific concerning the events following the fall of Srebrenica. Do you recall the date that the enclave fell, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you attend a meeting with VRS officers shortly after that?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you please describe how that meeting came about and the details of that meeting for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, on the 12th of July, 1995, in the evening hours and through UNPROFOR, or to be more precise, through Mr. Dudnik, I think that Avdo was informed that the Serbian side was interested in discussions. We as the War Presidency tried to agree on what to do that night. We asked the Main Staff of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina for authorisation, and we also asked the political leadership in Sarajevo for such authorisation. And we agreed to hold discussions with the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was agreed that I should go to the meeting, and Mr. Mujo Omanovic. The meeting was to be held and was held at check-point number 2 at Boksanica. We reached Boksanica in an UNPROFOR vehicle, and General Tolimir, Zdravko Tolimir, was there to greet us from the Serbian side, and the commander of the Rogatica brigade of the army of Republika Srpska. I think his rank was that of a Colonel, and his name was Rajko Pusic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt you, sir, with a couple of follow-ups, and I see that the translation here has translated the Colonel's name as Rajko Pusic. Is that the correct name, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's a K, not a P. Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just briefly, sir. If you could just orient the Trial Chamber. Where in relation to the town of Zepa is Boksanica located?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boksanica is to the south of the Zepa enclave. It's in the direction of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Mr. Omanovic whom you mentioned, what position, if any, did he hold?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he had a position of some kind in the Executive Board, in one of the bodies, but I can't remember. He held a position of some kind but it wasn't a high-level one. But he was a local man from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you would please continue describing for the Chamber this meeting that was held on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting General Tolimir more or less said that Srebrenica had fallen and that it was Zepa's turn now. He put forward, so to speak, two options: The complete evacuation of the entire population, or if we didn't agree to that the military option or, rather, a military solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did you have any questions for General Tolimir about who was included in the whole population?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the key issue. As far as I can remember, I asked General Tolimir if that meant that a 35-year-old man could get on a bus and leave the Zepa enclave together with his family, and General Tolimir said, "Yes, of course."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how was the departure of the entire population of Zepa supposed to occur according to General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the people would be evacuated in buses from Zepa to territory under the control of the ABiH. I don't know if any locations were mentioned. It was Olovo or Kladanj, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether he made any references to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, apart from the fact that at the beginning he said that Srebrenica had fallen and that it was now Zepa's turn. It was said that Zepa was no longer to remain such as it had been up until that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you clarify that at all, sir, what you mean by "such as it had been up until that point in time"?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I meant that it had the status of a protected area, a safe haven.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, can you estimate how long this meeting lasted?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. It didn't last for very long. I think it lasted between 40 minutes and 1 hour. That's a guess, but it was a long time ago so I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you could characterise, sir, who did most of the talking in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Zdravko Tolimir did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, were you authorised to provide an answer at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we weren't authorised. We agreed to see what was correct and to see what the Serbian side was asking for or proposing. I informed General Tolimir of this fact, and we agreed that we would return to Zepa. I and Mr. Mujo Omanovic would return. And this request or proposal would be relayed to the Zepa War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you in fact meet with the War Presidency, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Upon returning from the meeting, we met with the Zepa War Presidency and conveyed this request made by Mr. Tolimir to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did you decide to do?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the discussion went on for a long time, and in the end the proposal wasn't accepted, and as far as I can remember, I don't remember all the details, but people were worried about whether what General Tolimir had promised would actually be done. Finally Colonel Avdic -- Alic Avdo, I apologise -- Palic Avdo conveyed this information to the UNPROFOR commander. He conveyed the information on the fact that the proposal had not been accepted. Mr. Dudnik, the UNPROFOR commander in Zepa, went to check-point number 2 and informed the Serbian side of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I just want to go back. Why didn't you agree? What concerns, if any, did you have about whether General Tolimir would make good on what he had told you?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, at that time Srebrenica had fallen and the overall situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina was such that few people trusted others to make good on their word. This was the general atmosphere, so to speak, among the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at this time, sir, had you and Zepa received any reports or rumours of what had happened at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that first day and on the second day, I think, there was no information until people started returning. They had tried to get through to Kladanj. They failed to do so, and then rumours started spreading among the population in Zepa. I never spoke to those people from Srebrenica directly, but through others I heard about those events and the attempt to move over from Srebrenica to Kladanj or Olovo, and this made the population of Zepa even more afraid. But as far as I can remember, on the 13th and the 14th none of those people had yet arrived in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you conveyed the War Presidency's decision to Colonel Dudnik, what was his reaction?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that too. According to what those who were present said, he seemed quite afraid. He thought that this was the wrong decision and that we should have agreed to General Tolimir's request.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military attacks on the Zepa enclave were soon launched, were rapidly launched by the Republika Srpska army. There was shelling, and there were infantry attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was being struck by the shelling, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, practically everything. The defence lines, the houses, the inhabited areas, the villages. Everything was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long did it continue?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attacks continued until the 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part I was the centre of Zepa at my workplace, so to speak. I had contacts with UNPROFOR because it was fairly close to the UNPROFOR headquarters in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time, sir, was there armed resistance by the Muslims of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Resistance had been organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time what was your role, if you could describe it for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to some distribution of assignments in the War Presidency I was put in charge of liaising with UNPROFOR. And as things went on, I had to liaise with the Serb side in order to find out a way in which we could evacuate and save the people. So I was in constant contact with UNPROFOR on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So did you attend another meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 19th of July, the Boksanica check-point issued some kind of summons - in fact, General Mladic did so - for us to come and negotiate. This was done over UNPROFOR radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we agreed that we should attend this meeting, and I and Mr. Benjamin Kulovac went to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who is Mr. Kulovac, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kulovac is a doctor, a medical doctor. He was born in Zepa, and before the war he worked and lived in Rogatica as a doctor, and before the war he came to Zepa to his house, and in fact he ran the hospital. He took care of the wounded and the sick and everybody who needed medical treatment. So he was a local man.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether or not General Mladic had summonsed Colonel Palic to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was the request. It was addressed to Colonel Palic. I don't know if my memory will serve me right. I'm not sure whether Palic was actually there at the UNPROFOR base or not, but the two of us were appointed to participate in this meeting with Mladic. In other words, I and Mr. Kulovac were chosen to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of whether Colonel Palic had any concerns about appearing in person at negotiations with the VRS outside the centre of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he did have concerns. In fact, I don't know whether he was there for this meeting at all, but for the first negotiations with General Tolimir I do know that Avdo said he was afraid to go to this meeting, and that is why I and Mr. Mujo Omanovic were finally chosen to go. Now, as for this meeting with General Mladic, I can't recall whether he was in the UNPROFOR compound at all when we were arranging for our departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about this meeting a little bit, sir. Can you tell the Trial Chamber who on the VRS side was there?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this meeting was attended by General Mladic, General Tolimir, Colonel Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And -- and what happened, sir, at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this meeting Mladic dictated the terms for the evacuation of the population from Zepa. He said it will be done in this order: First the wounded, the women, the children, and the elderly. And as for the men of military age or able-bodied men, he wanted them to lay down their arms and to come to the UNPROFOR compound or something like that. This is how this particular request was worded. And then they were to be exchanged for the Serb soldiers. So these were his general terms dictated by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he wanted the civilian population to go?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific or clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did General Mladic identify anywhere in particular that he had in mind that the civilian population was to be transported to out of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Olovo or Kladanj were the two locations, and this is where people were later evacuated to. The civilian population, I mean. This territory was controlled by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did he say anything about buses, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, he said that he would provide the buses to transport the population the very next day. I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what did you do after this meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this meeting we went back to Zepa, and at that time we realised that we had nothing else to do, so it was quite clear that we would have to accept the evacuation of the civilian population. And from that time on until the 27th of July, the key problem was in fact the fate of the men of military age. We went back to Zepa, and we immediately got in touch with our leadership, the political leadership of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time in Sarajevo. We relayed to them Mladic's demands, and we asked them to find some way to ensure that the military age from -- men from Zepa would be exchanged with the captured Serb soldiers. And the military-aged men from Zepa were not supposed to go to UNPROFOR and surrender there, but they were supposed to be taken out of the enclave by helicopter and then exchanged for the Serb soldiers who had been captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So after this meeting on July 19th, do you recall what answer, if any, the leadership from Zepa gave to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really remember that any written or oral reply had been made, at least not for my part, but these delaying tactics and failure to create the conditions for the evacuation as requested by General Mladic, this was taken as our refusal of their proposal by the Serbs. Up until that time the Serbs did not really advance that much in military terms. The lines that were established at the beginning on the 13th of July remained in place, but then the attacks continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you're saying then, just to be clear, that the attacks continued after the 19th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you --

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact they may have been even more intense on some axes than they had been until that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how long this attack lasted?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this attack lasted for the next three days, three or four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, what was being struck during this attack?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, family houses, apartment buildings were targeted, as well as lines held by the soldiers. I even saw that at one point, I don't know what date it was, that the UNPROFOR headquarters in Zepa was hit. Incendiary bullets hit the roof of the school building where UNPROFOR had its headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention to the 24th of July, sir. Did you attend a third meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I attended the third meeting too. This time I was on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Trial Chamber that meeting and how it came about and what happened?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometime around the 23rd the key summit defending Zepa from the southern side Brezova Ravan fell. The Republika Srpska army for all intents and purposes established new lines that were very close to the centre of Zepa, and in military terms it was impossible to organise the defence to defend the centre of Zepa any more, and the request to renew negotiations came through UNPROFOR from General Mladic, and all attacks on all front lines ceased in this period. And this time I went to attend these negotiations alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was there on the VRS side, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the VRS side was again represented by General Mladic, General Tolimir, as far as I can remember. I think Colonel Rajko Kusic was also there, and some other officers whom I did not know. I had never seen them or encountered them at any of the meetings that preceded this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So please tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I arrived at the same check-point where I had already been twice. That was an UNPROFOR check-point, and there at the table -- in fact, this all took place outdoors. It was not inside any building. There was some tables there, and there was a piece of paper on the table. General Mladic sat at the other side. He was quite angry. He said that I had to sign this piece of paper, that there was no other solution. I can't remember some of the details because I was rather stressed. I read what was on the paper, and there were two key demands in this document, the evacuation of the population and the surrender of men of military age. Now, as to whether they should first surrender to UNPROFOR or directly to the Republika Srpska army, I can't remember this aspect, but I said that I was not authorised to sign anything on behalf of the army. I don't recall all the details, but it was our goal to start evacuating the population because it was impossible to defend the area any more. The population had already gone to the mountain. They retreated there. I signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, by the time of this meeting on the 24th, what information had you received, if any, about the events following the collapse of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Rumours had already begun circulating among the people there about the terrible events as they described it. I don't remember the details, but I did hear some of the stories. And this made the people in Zepa even more afraid, so the overall atmosphere in this period was one of fear almost bordering on panic among the population. People didn't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let's take a look at this agreement that you signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may have 6D00030 on e-court, please. And if it's possible to have the English translation on the split. Okay. Perhaps we can -- can we use the ELMO at the same time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It seems that we can't do a split scene, Your Honour, for the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why? All right. Okay. Okay. All right. Okay. Okay. It's okay. No problem. Let's put the English version on the ELMO. It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we could please move up the document on the ELMO, please, to show...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Are we looking at the English version or -- okay. I can see the -- I can see the translation too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this -- this document?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do, because I was given a copy after it was signed, but I don't remember what happened with it afterwards. I don't know if I gave it to somebody in the War Presidency in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that since that day you've never seen an original signed version of the document? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Does this appear to be, though, a fair translation, reproduction of that agreement, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say. The key points are here, but I don't know whether any corrections had been made. I couldn't really tell you without first looking at the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want to show you paragraph 7 of this document, sir. If you would just take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could do a -- can we do a split screen with the B/C/S or no split screen period? Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a problem, a technical problem, that Madam Registrar is encountering. So I think we need to work with the ELMO as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll take it one paragraph -- or one page at a time and perhaps I can facilitate it by just reading. It's a short paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, you need to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, paragraph 7 -- paragraph 7 begins on the English translation: "The civilians from Zepa shall enjoy freedom of choice of place of living and," this continues onto the second page, "residence in accordance with the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949 and the Additional Protocols from 1977." Sir, based on your meeting that day with General Mladic, is that paragraph 7 true, that the civilians from Zepa were to enjoy freedom of choice of place of living and residence?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was not discussed at all as things progressed. No one, in fact, even mentioned this possibility. But I do have to say that this -- the atmosphere there was quite specific among the people in Zepa. There was this fear. So that's -- this paragraph was there. It was put on the paper, but at that time and at that place it didn't really mean anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think we're done with this document for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like -- I'm sorry, but in this document my name is misspelled. I will not now mention my name, but in the heading itself my first name is misspelled, and then in the body of the text my last name is misspelled. So I would just like to -- for that to be on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification, Witness. During this -- during this meeting on the 24th of July, did General Mladic tell you anything else about how matters were going to proceed from that point on, particularly in terms of your role, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What he said, and it's not in this document, is that the entire operation relating to the evacuation of the population from Zepa would be carried out by General Tolimir together with Colonel Avdo Palic. They would be in the centre of Zepa and organise things so that the population could be transported. As for the security for the life of General Tolimir, well, I was supposed to go to check-point 2 and spend the entire period of time at that check-point as a guarantee for his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And with -- with all the military advances that the VRS had made up to this point, sir, why did General Tolimir need any guarantees for his safety?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that on the 24th there was a cease-fire, too, but the Republika Srpska army, as far as I know, hadn't entered the centre of Zepa. So there was that area in which there were no VRS soldiers. So reaching the centre meant passing through territory that wasn't under the control of the VRS of the Republika Srpska army. That's probably why things were done in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So what did you do next, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to Zepa, conveyed the information to the War Presidency, and that evening I think we had contact again with local leadership of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo. We informed the population. I'm not quite sure of the course of events, but we informed the population that an agreement had been reached on the evacuation of the civilian population and that those who wanted to could appear on the following day, on the 25th of July, in the centre of Zepa in order to be registered before entering buses and before being moved to territory outside of Zepa, to Kladanj or Olovo, to the places that had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, one of the terms that you said General Mladic had dictated to you was that the wounded were to be taken out first. Did you take any measures upon your return to Zepa in that regard, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I conveyed this information to Benjamin Kulovac, a doctor, and he immediately -- or, rather, on the following morning organised the transport of the wounded who weren't in the centre of Zepa. There was a makeshift hospital in the centre of Zepa. It was the clinic building, and these wounded were outside the centre of Zepa in a village or house which was somewhat sheltered from the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know why this hospital was located outside the centre of town, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because of the shelling of the centre. It wasn't possible to get through and establish contact with the wounded normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any idea when that hospital was -- was moved out to this other location?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know the exact date. I assume it was at the same time as the fall of Srebrenica. Perhaps on the 13th or 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, this brings us to the 25th of July, sir. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, as far as I can remember I was in Zepa, and General Tolimir also came escorted by two soldiers or officers. I can't remember exactly. And then there was a team from the International Red Cross that was also present. Technical details were discussed with General Tolimir by our Colonel Palic Bata [as interpreted], and the first buses arrived in Zepa. I think it was in the afternoon about 12.00, and the evacuation commenced. The names of the people getting on the buses were recorded, were put on a list, and I believe that the list was also provided to the representatives of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did you, sir, in fact see Generals -- General Tolimir and Colonel Palic moving about freely in the centre of Zepa at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did they in fact leave on one of the convoys on the 25th, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the last convoy that was organised that day. Colonel Palic evacuated his family in that convoy, his wife and children, and as far as I know, he also escorted that convoy as far as Kladanj, and on the following day he returned to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about General Tolimir, sir? Do you know how he left in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Tolimir, together with Colonel Avdic [sic], left Zepa in that same convoy. Night was falling. It was already dark at the time. So it was in the same convoy. It's possible that [sic] sat down together with General Tolimir in the vehicle that Tolimir was in at least when leaving Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just what type of vehicle was it, sir, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a personnel carrier. It was an armoured vehicle but not a heavy armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, I see in the transcript a couple of references to a Colonel Avdic. Were you referring to Colonel Palic, sir, just so the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a mistake. I apologise. Colonel Avdo Palic. I must have got a bit mixed up. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I just want to ask you some more specific questions about what you observed with respect to these convoys on the 25th. Do you recall seeing any VRS soldiers participating in or assisting these transportations on the 25th, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the very centre of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. I can only remember the individuals who were escorting General Tolimir. As far as I can remember, they were wearing uniforms of the VRS. As to whether they were assisting or not, I really can't remember since I did not really participate much in the process of preparing the population for their evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. On the 25th do you recall whether you saw any UNPROFOR soldiers participating in these transportations?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. They were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did you observe any mistreatment of the Muslim civilian population as they boarded these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no mistreatment, apart from the fact that sometimes the desire to come first caused a bit of a shuffle, but there were no cases of abuse. Everything went smoothly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who supplied these vehicles? And if you could also describe what kind of vehicles we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the vehicles for the evacuation were provided by General Mladic. The evacuation was carried out as follows: As far as the type of vehicle is concerned, from Zepa to Boksanica - Boksanica's a check-point to the south of Zepa in the direction of Rogatica - transport on that route was carried out -- or, rather, the people were transported in buses and open lorries along that route. And from Boksanica the people who were in these open lorries were put onto buses. So from Boksanica they were evacuated in the direction of Kladanj in buses alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, on the 25, sir, did you attend yet another meeting?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the afternoon I met General Mladic again, this time at Brezova Ravan, a location closer to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what happened at the meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember nothing of much significance happened. There was some discussion about the evacuation, and after that I returned to Zepa again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any recollection of meeting General Rupert Smith at some point on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember two meetings. I'm sure of one at a meeting with General Rupert Smith -- there was a meeting at Boksanica with General Rupert Smith at the same location where we had previously had meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. At this time if we could be shown P02493. It's a map. It -- if it gets shrunk on the e-court we have a copy for the ELMO if we need to resort to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have an image in front of you on the computer?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you read it adequately, or would you prefer to have it on the ELMO? It's up to you at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'd also ask if anybody else is having any problems with legibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's very difficult to read except what appears to be in bold letters. This is better.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's perfect, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the areas this map depicts?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you to mark two locations, if you would, with the help of Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which locations should I mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see a location marked Brezova Ravan? And before you mark anything, I'd just ask you --

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall with any more precision where this location in which you met General Mladic on the 25th of July was? Can you mark that on the map?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you can just mark that with an X, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you may need to -- we may need to move the image slightly, but I would also ask you to mark the location of the Boksanica check-point where you attended these meetings.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I'll be mistaken. It's this point here at the very border between this precipice and plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you've marked that with a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Witness, to the right of where you put an X near Brezova Ravan, could you please write the initials RM.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where you put the other sign, could you to the right please put the initials CK -- BCK [sic]. Yeah, BCP. CP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] BCP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. Don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, the -- the dotted line on which you've laid this oval where you've marked this check-point at Boksanica, can you just indicate what that is? The dotted line that runs from the marking at Brezova Ravan down to that check-point.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a local road that one drives along. It was part of the route used to move the population out.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you would just put today's date in any of the corners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we don't broadcast -- from this point onwards we don't broadcast. He puts his signature -- he puts his signature and the date, please, but we are not broadcasting it. So in any of the corners, I suggest bottom right corner, you put -- you sign your name and put the date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think we can save this document and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this brings us to the 26th of July. Can you describe what -- what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th of July in the morning, Colonel Avdo Palic came to see me and said he had returned from Kladanj where he had evacuated his family, and when returning he had a brief meeting with General Mladic at Boksanica. Mladic had requested that I go to check-point number 2, the guarantee for the safety, for the life of General Tolimir, who was continuing with the evacuation of the population from Zepa on that day. I went to Boksanica with the first convoy and stayed there for the following two days until the 27th of July, until the end of the 27th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, prior to leaving Zepa for Boksanica can you describe for the Trial Chamber what was going on with the civilian population in the Zepa area and what you saw happening in Zepa town?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th quite a few number of civilians or only a few civilians had decided to move out. They went to certain closer -- areas closer to the centre of Zepa and followed what was going on on the 26th before I went to Boksanica. A significant part of the population of Zepa had gathered their most essential items, put them in bags of various kinds and came to request that they participate in the evacuation. There was a big crowd, and it was difficult to witness all these events. So this was on the 26th. Everyone wanted to leave as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to congregating in the centre of Zepa, where had the civilian population been for the last several days?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was to the north if you have a look at the map. To the south of the river of Zepa there were these people who had to leave these places because they'd been taken by the VRS. They were in the mountain or three, four, five kilometres from the centre of Zepa. There was some caves or huts or other buildings for accommodation, and part of the population had not yet left their houses, so those inhabitants left their houses and came to the centre of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge had -- had there been any larger gathering area outside of Zepa town where civilians had gathered?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of the centre of Zepa, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I see it's 10.30. I don't know if this is a good time to take the first recess, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You shouldn't think, you should know that it is the right time. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, is it -- is it fair to say that the bulk of the transportations really began and happened on the 26th of July?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, bulk of the transportations, yes, but there were one or two convoys on the 25th of July, as far as I know. The first convoy was the convoy with the wounded, and its destination was Sarajevo. The second convoy was the convoy with the civilian population, and it headed towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, from what you saw on the 25th and the 26th, can you describe the -- the emotional state of the civilians as they were getting onto the buses? I think you've spoken a little bit about it already, but just briefly if you can could encapsulate the emotional state that you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all the people that were to be transported were afraid. There was a lot of uncertainty because families got split. In other words, men of military age did not accompany their wives and children, and I'm sure you will understand that this was a very difficult situation in emotional terms for everybody involved. And generally speaking, all of them were afraid, in fear of what would happen to their fathers, husbands. So fear, uncertainty, perhaps even some panic. So that was the emotional state, in general terms, of the population that was to be transported.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, on the 26th of July did you observe any mistreatment of the civilian population as they were being transported?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The transportation went on smoothly, and there was no mistreatment. Everything was done in accordance with the agreement that had been reached -- or, rather, that had been dictated by General Mladic and then put on paper. There was no mistreatment. Everything went smoothly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during this period of time from, say, the 13th all the way up to the next day, the 27th, can you describe how often you were in contact with Colonel Palic?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had contact with him a few -- few times. Three or four times. I saw him very briefly, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you've already told us that on that day, the 26th, you went to Boksanica. What did you do when you got there?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spent most of the time there in General Mladic's company. We were sitting there at this table, and there was some general discussion on other topics, and every convoy that would arrive from Zepa, as far as I can remember, was visited by General Mladic. He would get on the buses. There was a relaxed atmosphere throughout this day. I'm talking about the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you met with General Smith at all on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The meeting that I can confirm was the meeting on the 26th. That was a meeting with General Smith. The -- we actually discussed the options for the removal of the men of military age from Zepa, because at previous meetings with General Smith, dealing with this topic should have been organised by the authorities in Sarajevo, the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you actually meet General Krstic that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I actually was introduced to General Krstic that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: By whom, and if you'd just describe that encounter for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was introduced to General Krstic by General Mladic. We were sitting at the table, and General Krstic was at another table, and at one point Mladic told me, pointing with his hand, this is General Krstic. And then he says, "Come here, Krle," which I guess was the nickname for him that General Mladic used. Krstic came to our table, and there we were introduced to each other, and General Mladic said that General Krstic was in charge of the military operations against Zepa. We exchanged a couple of sentences, something to the effect that we were from the same area because I, too, was born in the Han Pijesak municipality, and I think I recall that General Krstic told me that he was -- had been born in the Vlasenica municipality, which is the municipality -- the neighbouring municipality. This lasted for just a very brief time and General Krstic went back to his table. At that time I didn't know who General Krstic was at all. Only later did I learn more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just briefly, did you notice anything about him physically?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a problem with his leg. I don't know whether it was the right or the left leg, and he had difficulty walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night of the 26th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the night at the check-point number 2, in a room where UNPROFOR soldiers slept. So I slept there together with them. Those were Ukrainian soldiers serving with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So that brings us to the 27th of July. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evacuation continued that day, and the last convoy to leave Zepa for Boksanica arrived, if I'm not mistaken, at around 1.00, 1.00 p.m., and the situation got tense then. General Mladic demanded that the troops surrender, and he detained the convoy there at Boksanica and refused his permission for the convoy to move on. And on this last convoy from Zepa there were the president of the War Presidency of Zepa, Mr. Mehmed Hajric, and the head of the civilian protection, Mr. Imamovic. We were asked -- so the three of us were now all in the same place, so the relaxed atmosphere was no more. The situation was now very tense, and a demand was made for one of us to go to the -- into the mountain near Zepa where there was a mass of men of military age. They were concentrated there. And they were to be told that they should surrender. And the person who got appointed to do this task, I don't remember whether General Mladic appointed the president of the War Presidency, Mr. Mehmed Hajric to do so or somebody else, but as far as I can remember, he went towards Zepa in an UNPROFOR vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The convoy was there all the time, and then around 6.00 or 7.00 p.m. I was ordered to go to one of the buses used to transport the civilians. This bus was there at Boksanica, and I spent maybe three hours there on this bus. And then at around 20.30 [as interpreted], in other words, in the evening, I was told by a soldier to come. And Amir Imamovic was on another bus, and we both were taken to the same room where I had spent the night in the UNPROFOR compound. There were already some UNPROFOR soldiers there. As far as I can remember, an approval was given at that time for the convoy to move on. The convoy was allowed to go. And then that night at around 11.30 p.m., soldiers came, Republika Srpska army soldiers, and told me and Amir that as of now we had the status of prisoners of war. We were handcuffed. They put a handcuff to one of my hands and then handcuffed Amir at the end other, and they took us out of this room. And during our arrest I really want to note that there were four or five UNPROFOR soldiers there, and the UNPROFOR commander for Zepa, Colonel Semjon Dudnik, was also there. Of course, they didn't do anything. We were first taken towards the woods and then we did a little detour and were finally taken back to the road to Borike where we got into a Republika Srpska army vehicle, and we were then taken to the hotel at Borike. And we slept there in a room. We -- the handcuffs had not been removed. In the morning the handcuffs were removed and we were given some breakfast, and we were taken back to Boksanica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 30, line 17, it should read "around 22.30."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, before we move on, sir, can you just describe generally and briefly where Borike is located?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Borike are halfway between Zepa and Rogatica. To the south of Zepa but further down from Boksanica. A lot farther down than Boksanica. Borike used to be a well-known tourist resort before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So that brings us to the 28th of July. What happened that day, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on that day in the morning we were again taken back to Boksanica. I saw General Mladic there again, but this time he didn't even say hello to me because I was already a prisoner. And then a security officer called me and he started asking me questions, where I was born, things like that. We had a little talk. It lasted maybe 20 minutes to half an hour. And then he was called away, and some 10 minutes after that we were put back in the car and Amir and I were then taken again to the hotel where we had spent the previous night.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you spent a couple of days at the hotel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We spent the next couple of days at the hotel at Borike.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date now, whether it was the 30th or sometime around the 30th of July, we were under VRS military police guard. They took us out, and they drove a Golf Mark 2, as we call it in Sarajevo, and Mehmed Hajric was taken out of another room, and Amir and I, we didn't know that he had been there. And so the three of us were taken to the prison in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long were you at this prison in Rogatica, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prison -- in fact, we left the prison in Rogatica on the 11th of January, 1996, and from there we went to Kula. It's yet another prison, this time in the vicinity of Sarajevo, controlled by the Republika Srpska army. We spent four days there before we were exchanged or released or whatever. I don't know what -- what definition was actually used in the Dayton agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you were first brought to this prison you told us that Mr. Hajric and Mr. Imamovic were brought there with you. Were they there for some period of time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the same room, I, Hajric, and Imamovic. As far as I can remember, in mid-August 1995, they were taken out of the room and they never got back.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And have you received any information concerning the fate or whereabouts of Mr. Imamovic and Mr. Hajric, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to information at my disposal, they were killed, and about a year ago their bodies were found and they were buried in Sarajevo. So both Mr. Imamovic and Mr. Hajric.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the last thing I'd like to do is view some video clips that we have available on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could call up V000-1355, and that's P02489, for the record. The segment begins at 9 minutes, 22 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I would ask that the video not be broadcast. I've had some consultations with my learned friends. I think that we'll have some identification issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That's clearly no problem so far as this is concerned because the protection that's been put in place means that it clearly can't now be broadcast. Let's perhaps take it in stages. So I've got no objection to that, and as I've said, I've discussed it with my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have transcripts in English and B/C/S. P02490. To this point there has not been any substantive discussion of any kind that's been transcribed. There are a couple of lines. The substantive translations begin at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to clear another thing. You've all heard Mr. Josse's statement. Does any other member of the Defence teams wish to comment? Okay. So we can proceed, and the rest of the video will not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The reason is that we have granted face distortion for -- for this witness, and it wouldn't make sense to show his face on video and then ask him if he recognises himself. Yes, Mr. Thayer. Sorry for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's all right, Your Honour. I'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we are on page 2 of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are on page 1 of 4 of the English transcript at line 16 is where the next segment begins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we're at -- we're at 11 minutes, 53.4 seconds. Just a couple of quick questions before we move on to the substance of the video. Can you tell the Court what day this footage is being shot?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 19th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the location, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNPROFOR check-point at Boksanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, there are three figures visible in this particular clip. Do you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Benjamin Kulovac in the middle. I'm on the left, and on the right I think this is Colonel Semjon Dudnik, but this screen shot is not very good so I can't really claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Now, the individual you've identified as Dr. Kulovac appears to have a white object in his hand. Can you just tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It's a white object. I don't know if it was a white cloth or anything -- or something like that, because as we approached the UNPROFOR check-point an agreement had been made before we actually headed out. This was to be a sign, a white flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just so -- just so the record is -- is clear, you are in the lighter coloured shirt to the left, facing the screen, of the individual with the white object; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you identify, based on your recollection of this meeting, who the individual wearing the cap with his back to the camera is?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's General Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this probably needs no real identification, but just for the record and -- can you identify the man at the far right of the frame?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we are at 12 minutes, 18.4 seconds. And we can continue, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've stop at 14 minutes, 57.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Thayer. Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I believe there is a mistake in the transcript. It's page 35, line 12. I'm sorry to have to go back somewhat. What is mentioned in the transcript is this was supposed to be a sign, a white flag, and what the witness said, I believe, is that it was a signal of recognition, that the white flag indicated that they were prepared to surrender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, have you followed -- thank you, Madam Fauveau. Have you followed what Madam Fauveau has just stated? Didn't you receive interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe there's a mistake here. What the witness had said was that it was a signal of recognition and not a white flag, which would have been to indicate that they were prepared to surrender.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you received interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And you agree with what Madam Fauveau has stated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I clarify this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The last interpretation was the correct one. It wasn't a white flag as a sign of surrender. It was a sign of recognition. That's what I had in mind, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Witness. Mr. Thayer, we have frozen the video at 14 minutes, 57.9 seconds. If you could proceed with your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the individual in the middle of this frame with his hand raised?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Colonel Semjon Dudnik, the UNPROFOR commander in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've stopped at 15 minutes, 17.7 seconds. Can you indicate any individuals whom you recognise in this still?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic is to the left. On the same side and by his side is General Tolimir. The others I cannot identify, but to the right there's Benjamin Kulovac, and I am sitting next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we may turn to V000-3412. That is P02491, and the transcripts for that are at P02492, and those transcripts will pick up immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've stopped at 45 minutes, 30 seconds. I ask you if you recognise any particular individual in this frame.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Somewhere in the middle you can see Colonel Avdo Palic. Should I point him out?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you can identify any article of clothing he appears to be wearing, sir, that would distinguish him from people around him.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has a military uniform -- or, rather, the top part of a military uniform on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in the frame's perspective is he standing to the right of a woman in a purple coloured kerchief or head wrap?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've stopped at 46 minutes and 1 second. Do you recognise anyone in this frame?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the then president of the War Presidency of Zepa municipality, Mr. Mehmed Hajric. He's in the foreground.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Wearing a light blue shirt or jacket of some kind, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think he's wearing a shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber where this footage was taken?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This footage was taken in the centre of Zepa, which is where the buses with the population departed from.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know what day this footage was taken?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was on the 25th or on the 26th. In the first part of the footage where you can see the wounded, I'm sure that was on the 25th of July. But as for the part that was shown a little later, perhaps it was on the 26th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could not broadcast the following portion, which will involve some meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Yes. We will not broadcast the following sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we've stopped at 46 minutes, 11 seconds. From viewing this video clip do you recognise anybody in this frame?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Benjamin Kulovac is in the left-hand corner. He is the only person I can recognise in this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about now, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Rupert Smith at the extreme right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we're at 46 minutes, 13.7 seconds. And that's the individual with the full profile to the camera; is that correct? Seated.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're at 46 minutes, 25.4 seconds. Do you recognise anybody in this frame, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Rupert Smith is to the left. In the middle it's General Krstic. And to the right, in the foreground, the person is General Ratko Mladic. Those are the persons I can identify in this frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what's your best recollection as to when this meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meeting was probably held on the 26th of July, 1995, at Boksanica. It's the 26th in my opinion, but I'm not a hundred per cent certain, but it's certain that it was when the evacuation had already started. So it was around the 25th, 26th, or 27th, but now I believe that it was the 26th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you haven't identified yourself in this video segment. What's your best recollection as to whether you were actually present for this meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was present. I can't be seen in this video footage, but I'm fairly certain that I also attended this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For the record, we're going to pick up at 49 minutes and 15 seconds, or as close thereto as we can get.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we're at 50 minutes, 14.8 seconds. Were these the types of buses and trucks that you testified seeing arriving at Boksanica on the 26th and 27th of July?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the trucks and buses. You can see a truck in this frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we're at 51 minutes, 23 seconds. What is your best recollection as to the day on which this footage was being shot?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first question is, is this something that should be removed, concealed?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe this is still not being broadcast based on the prior request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I imagined. I mean -- okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, sir, what's your best recollection as to the day this footage is being filmed?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was on the 26th of July, 1995, when CNN was one of the teams that came to Boksanica. My surname has been misspelled here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to redact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry, I was in the old mode, Mr. President, forgive me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's redact and proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise anyone in this still, 51 minutes, 23 seconds?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am to the right, and the person to the left of me is a gentleman from CNN. He was the head of some sort of a team, a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at 53 minutes, 15.5 seconds, can you recognise who the man is sitting to General Mladic's left or to the right of the frame?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's Colonel Semjon Dudnik. The colonel and the UNPROFOR commander in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, sir, were you alone by yourself on the other side of this table from General Mladic and Colonel Dudnik?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was sitting opposite General Mladic, directly opposite General Mladic, and this last question was put to me by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just a couple of final questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, if -- we can go back into full broadcast, or if there's anything else we need to do, but I think we're -- we've remained in open session so, as I understand it, there's nothing more to make it public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, during these clips, for example when you're alone across the table from General Mladic, were being interviewed by the reporter by yourself, what were your -- what were your concerns? What were your -- your main worries at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time my main concern was about the fate of the able-bodied men of Zepa. All the negotiations, everything what General Mladic also said had to do with finding a solution or a way of exchanging the able-bodied men from Zepa for members of the VRS army. But there was one condition that the able-bodied men from Zepa always established. They wouldn't first surrender to the VRS army. The idea was that helicopter transport should perhaps be organised by UNPROFOR, but obviously this remained just an idea. The main problem was what would happen to the able-bodied men from Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And why wouldn't they first surrender to the VRS army, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's clear there was fear. They were afraid that people would be killed, that they wouldn't survive. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, during this entire period of time from the -- let's say the 19th through the 27th when you were at this UNPROFOR check-point in Boksanica, who appeared to you to be in control of that check-point?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially it was an UNPROFOR check-point, a check-point that was manned by the international forces, but it was actually under the control of the VRS army with General Mladic at its head. The UNPROFOR soldiers would move away, and the check-point was in fact used as a temporary headquarters for General Mladic when he was present in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Thayer. Before you start, Mr. Josse - I take it that you are going first - let's try and revise the time estimate required for cross-examination. I have listed you as requiring two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think I need at least that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I have the Miletic Defence team require two hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. For now we are still estimating two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I have the Beara team asking for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Slightly under one hour, Your Honour, but I think if we could be safe, as an estimate, 45 minutes to an hour, but it all depends on obviously the other questions. It may get shortened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the others I'm not worried about. Ten minutes, 10 minutes, and 20 minutes. All right. Mr. Josse. We will have a break in 20 minutes' time, and then you have the last session all for yourself, and we will continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'd like to begin, Witness, if I may, asking about the actual evacuation on the 25th, 26th, 27th of July that you've just been describing to the Trial Chamber, and you have been at pains to point out in answer to questions from Mr. Thayer that there was no maltreatment of those that were leaving. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But what I'm going to ask you is to paint us a picture of who exactly was there, and let's begin with who was there from the VRS. You've told us that General Tolimir was there, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Tolimir was in the centre of Zepa, and the convoys first came to Boksanica. They stopped there for a while, and then they continued on to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And it was in the centre of Zepa that the evacuees boarded the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buses and open trucks because the road to Zepa is quite bad, quite rough. So there were both buses and open trucks in Zepa, and when they came -- when the open trucks came to Boksanica, they were transferred onto buses, which means that from Boksanica on, all the people were transported on buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So General Tolimir was there and he was accompanied by some lower-ranking officers of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA TORLAK [Resumed]
